subject.title: [Feature]: REST endpoint for session management in HTTP API integrations

question: Should OpenClaw expose a narrow public `/v1/sessions/*` HTTP session-management API for OpenAI-compatible integrations, or keep session controls behind WebSocket/native clients and explicitly approved admin surfaces?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but reset, compaction, model, and reasoning mutations over HTTP change the trusted operator boundary and need maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve narrow `/v1/sessions/*` API
options.body: Implement reset/status/compact/model/reasoning endpoints with explicit scope mapping, strict schemas, tests, docs, and no slash-command re-enablement.

options.title: Limit HTTP to reset/status first
options.body: Ship only the most common reset/status workflow while deferring compaction and model/reasoning mutations until the security model is proven.

options.title: Keep controls off `/v1`
options.body: Document WebSocket/native clients or an intentionally enabled admin surface as the supported control plane for trusted automation.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow `/v1/sessions/*` API
recommendation.body: Implement reset/status/compact/model/reasoning endpoints with explicit scope mapping, strict schemas, tests, docs, and no slash-command re-enablement.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits on the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` HTTP surface that vincentkoc recently added and documented.
